newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan vows Islamist return to power.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan vows Islamist return to power.

text.p: Turkey's former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday the new secularist coalition would fail to win a confidence vote, opening the way for his Islamists to return to power.
Parliament is scheduled to hold a vote of confidence on July 12 in the anti-Islamist government formed on Monday by conservative Mesut Yilmaz.
"In 12 days parliament will fulfill a historical duty, it will turn its back on anti-democratic forces," Erbakan told his Welfare Party deputies in parliament.
"After the loss of these 12 days a government compatible with democracy will be established," he said.
Erbakan resigned last month in the hope that his party could stay in power in a revamped coalition led by conservative Tansu Ciller.
But President Suleyman Demirel named Yilmaz as prime minister on Monday in an attempt to deny power to the Islamists after months of political chaos.
A wave of defections from Ciller's party has boosted Yilmaz's chances of winning the vote in parliament.
The new government, a minority coalition supported by a left-wing party, has around a dozen more MPs on paper than its opponents in the 550-member national assembly.
